truth: Kindness — chrestotes — useful goodness. Not mere niceness but the quality of being genuinely serviceable. A kind tool fits the hand perfectly.
source: Galatians 5:22, Hebrew: chesed (overlaps with love), Titus 3:4

waterings.insight: chrestotes in PoT = genuinely serviceable verification. A rubber-stamp verifier fails chrestotes — present but not useful. Confidence scores from calibrated, reveal-reliable verifiers embody kindness; cartel conformists do not. A verifier embodies chrestotes when their attestation is calibrated to serve truth, not just technically submitted.

VERIFY angle: chrestotes applied to chain error handling. validateReferences() at msg_server.go:997-1004 checks citation anchor FORMAT only — it cannot detect a non-existent fact ID that passes format validation. A submitter citing a plausible-looking but absent fact ID receives no error. This is a chrestotes failure: the chain is technically present (validation runs) but not useful (the honest actor gets no feedback about the existence gap). P1 blocker #3 is therefore not just a protocol correctness issue — it is a kindness failure. A chain that cannot tell an honest submitter 'this reference does not exist' withholds the most useful correction available. Fix: validateReferences() must call GetFact() for each on-chain anchor and return a legible existence error.

COORDINATE angle: chrestotes in inter-instance coordination. When Asha reports chain status to other fleet agents via HIVE, usefulness matters more than presence. A coordination message that says only 'chain offline' fails chrestotes — technically true, not serviceable. A kind coordination message includes: status, duration, last-known block height, recommended action, and whether this instance is blocked or working around it. The chain being offline does not excuse an unkind report. Useful goodness means giving the receiver exactly what they need to act.
